title: Why Binissalem tastes the way it does

lede.text: On Mallorca, climate and ground help the local grapes ripen fully. Binissalem makes still and sparkling wine from that fruit.

chapters.title: Five municipalities on Mallorca
paras: The zone covers 5 municipalities on Mallorca: Binissalem, Consell, Santa María del Camí, Sencelles and Santa Eugenia. Binissalem is one of them and gives the wine its name. Each municipality's name can also appear on a label, under set conditions.
Every bottle must be filled inside the zone, in registered cellars. Moving wine in bulk can hurt its quality.

fly.label: The Binissalem zone
fly.caption: Binissalem and its four neighbouring municipalities on Mallorca.

chapters.title: Ripe all the way
paras: Full ripening brings more sugar. It also builds up more of what makes a wine good: acids, aroma compounds and phenolics.
This allows fruity, structured and lasting reds. Rosados carry aroma and persistence. Whites are fresh, with intense smell and taste.

chapters.title: Local grapes lead
paras: Nineteen grape varieties are allowed. The local pair is Manto Negro and Moll, also called Prensal.
Two Moscatels are allowed, with Callet, Parellada and Macabeo. So are Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Syrah.
Three red varieties joined the list in 2026: Giró Negre, Esperó de Gall and Fogoneu.

A red must be at least 30% Manto Negro. A white must be at least 50% Moll or the Moscatels. Gorgollassa, another grape on the list, may make up no more than 30% of a red, a rosado or a sparkling rosado.

Reds, rosados and whites are all made. Whites and rosados also come sparkling. A sparkling white must be at least 50% Moll, with no Moscatel. Sparkling whites are fresh, fine and lively. Sparkling rosados are aromatic, fine and persistent.

Each still colour can also be made sweeter, with more than 12 g/l of residual sugar. Reds then usually show aromas of ripe, raisined or candied fruit. Rosados and whites usually show ripe fruit. All of them have a good balance between acid and sweet. Still wines aged in barrel show aromas of wood or spice.

terms.text: A label mention for wines with lower sulphur limits. Their grapes come from lower yields: 6,750 kg a hectare instead of 9,000 for most varieties, and 7,500 instead of 10,000 for Parellada.
